When every changed path matches the project\\u0027s non-executable set, the build and test gates are skipped and a VerificationSkipped fact is recorded on the run stream naming every changed path and the rule each one matched, shown by h9k task show in the gate rendering where a pass shows today. A skip is never a pass for scoping: the next gate run that actually runs takes its scope from the last real VerificationPassed, never from a skip\u0022,\u0022The non-executable set is per project: h9k project set --non-executable-path \\u003Cglob\\u003E, repeatable, with default restoring the compiled set, listed by h9k project show. The compiled default is exactly four rules: any *.md file, docs/, .claude/skills/, and .claude/commands/. Any changed path outside the set runs the gates as today, a diff that mixes code and content runs the gates in full, and a project can only add to the set, never remove a rule from the default\u0022,\u0022The skip applies at every entry into the gates on a run: first delivery, the verify pass between review cycles, and every follow-up lap, so a fix lap on a content-only branch does not pay the gates either; each entry classifies afresh and records its own fact\u0022,\u0022CI on GitHub is untouched: the pull request still runs the repository\\u0027s workflow as it does today; this is a local-gate optimization only\u0022,\u0022Tests prove: a content-only diff skips with a fact naming every path and rule; a mixed diff runs the gates in full; a path outside the set runs the gates; a project-added glob is honored and a default rule cannot be removed; a fix lap on a content-only branch skips again; a skip is never used as a scope base.
